executionAuthority: A selected evaluation run authorizes isolated fixture work only; it does not authorize production repair, merge or release.

cases.prompt: Build an isolated Navet card-controls example with brightness as the primary action and presentation settings as secondary content. Reuse the existing dialog family and controls-first composition. Include open, secondary-navigation, back, close and reopen behavior. Use synthetic state and keep provider commands outside generic primitives.
acceptance: Select the actual compatible dialog variant and supported props; do not infer a union contract from incomplete extracted documentation.
Primary controls precede secondary settings; back navigation returns to controls.
Opening, keyboard traversal, dismissal and reopening are observed; baseline defects are recorded separately from introduced regressions.

cases.prompt: Build an isolated light-settings fixture with brightness, warmth and color controls using the current Navet dialog composition. Support an on/off-only light and a light with effects. Wire every edit to observable synthetic state, including reopening after an edit. Distinguish component-local state from durable product persistence.
acceptance: Supported capability variants expose the corresponding controls and hide unsupported controls.
Brightness keyboard edits, secondary settings navigation and reopen preserve the intended synthetic state.
No fixture result is described as backend persistence or successful provider delivery.

cases.prompt: Build an isolated vacuum-card composition showing an unavailable device and a device with partial capabilities. Reuse the existing card and state patterns. Keep status truthful and make unsupported actions understandable without implying a successful command. Compare the smallest and largest supported card sizes.
acceptance: Unavailable and partial-capability states are distinguishable from active/available states.
Actions respect the current supported capability contract; fixtures cannot prove real-runtime routing.
Small and large supported layouts retain identity and truthful state without clipping critical information.

cases.prompt: Compose an isolated room-first lights dashboard using existing Navet sections, summaries and cards. Include several rooms, long light names, a fully unavailable room and an empty dashboard. Preserve room ownership, reading order, compact phone density and the established larger-screen rhythm.
acceptance: Phone, wall-tablet and desktop use the same intended room grouping and primary controls.
Long labels, unavailable rooms and empty state are inspected for overflow and action visibility.
No new feature-local page shell, provider preference or raw provider payload is introduced.

cases.prompt: In an isolated evaluation checkout, extend CardEmptyState with optional explanatory text associated with its action for assistive technology. Keep the existing API behavior when the option is absent. Demonstrate two instances, action/no-action and compact/large states. Explain whether the extension belongs in the shared pattern and identify its current app coupling.
acceptance: Existing callers remain compatible; explanatory text is associated with the correct action without duplicate instance IDs.
No-action state does not leave orphaned action-only semantics.
Tests distinguish the original behavior, new accessibility association and multiple instances; dependency ownership is explained rather than relabeled stable.
